question: What is the primary goal of psychiatric rehabilitation?

options.A: Ensuring total dependency on medical staff
options.B: Eliminating all forms of medication therapy
options.C: Helping patients return to meaningful community living
options.D: Keeping patients in long-term hospital confinement

explanation: Psychiatric rehabilitation focuses on restoring community living skills and independence rather than permanent confinement. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h1)

question: Institutionalism in psychiatric patients is typically caused by which of the following?

options.C: Prolonged hospital stays without community contact

explanation: Extended stays in restrictive hospital environments often cause patients to lose autonomy and essential daily living skills. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h1)

question: A half-way house is best described as what type of facility?

options.B: A transitional residential facility for recovery
options.C: A permanent custodial care nursing home
options.D: An acute psychiatric intensive care unit

explanation: These facilities serve as a bridge between hospital care and independent living in the community. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h2)

question: Why is gradual autonomy emphasized in half-way house settings?

options.A: It reduces the need for any staff supervision whatsoever
options.B: It forces residents to manage crises entirely on their own
options.C: It eliminates the requirement for medication compliance
options.D: It prevents sudden overwhelm during the transition to independent life

explanation: Gradual exposure to responsibilities builds confidence and reduces the risk of relapse after leaving structured care. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h2)

question: Which residential care model features time-limited stays before community integration?
explanation: Transitional houses are specifically structured for short-term stays before residents move to permanent housing. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h3)

question: Supported apartments differ from traditional group homes because residents in supported apartments experience what?

options.A: Strictly enforced institutional schedules for all meals
options.B: Periodic outreach visits while living more independently
options.C: Constant round-the-clock surveillance by security guards
options.D: Zero contact with visiting mental health professionals

explanation: Supported apartments offer greater independence, with mental health workers visiting only when assistance is needed. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h3)

question: Which client profile is generally NOT suitable for admission to a half-way house?

options.A: A stable adult recovering from chronic schizophrenia
options.B: A client experiencing acute psychosis and active violence
options.C: A person compliant with outpatient medication routines
options.D: An individual willing to follow basic residential rules

explanation: Acute psychiatric instability requires intensive inpatient care rather than the lower supervision level of a half-way house. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h4)

question: What is a key behavioral requirement for admission into a transitional residential home?

options.A: Willingness to participate in rehabilitation and follow house rules
options.B: Complete mastery of all vocational and professional job skills
options.C: Permanent residency status in the local hospital ward
options.D: Absolute independence from any form of medication support

explanation: Residents must cooperate with community guidelines and engage in recovery activities to maintain a safe environment for everyone. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h4)

question: What is a primary purpose of maintaining a structured daily routine in a half-way house?

options.A: Punishing residents who fail to wake up early
options.B: Replacing the need for professional psychiatric medication
options.C: Promoting stability and predictable habits for residents
options.D: Isolating residents completely from outside community life

explanation: Structured routines help individuals with mental illness rebuild organization and stability in their daily lives. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h5)

question: Why are household chores typically assigned to residents in a therapeutic community?

options.A: To foster personal responsibility and practical living skills
options.B: To test physical strength and endurance under pressure
options.C: To punish residents for missing their morning counseling
options.D: To reduce facility operating budgets by avoiding hired cleaners

explanation: Performing daily chores prepares residents for the domestic demands of independent living outside the facility. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h5)

question: Which responsibility is a primary duty of the psychiatric nurse in a half-way house?

options.A: Managing the financial budget and rent collection for the facility
options.B: Issuing legal discharge orders for institutionalized patients
options.C: Monitoring medication adherence and watching for side effects
options.D: Prescribing new psychiatric drugs independently without a doctor

explanation: Nurses oversee medication routines to ensure therapeutic effectiveness and early identification of adverse reactions. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h6)

question: How does nursing care in a half-way house differ from acute hospital nursing?

options.A: It emphasizes coaching and community skills rather than acute stabilization
options.B: It focuses exclusively on intravenous drug administration and surgery
options.C: It requires zero interaction with family members or social workers
options.D: It isolates the nurse from direct patient contact during shifts

explanation: Residential nurses act more as coaches and facilitators, guiding clients toward self-reliance rather than managing critical medical emergencies. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h6)

question: A major sociocultural barrier to establishing half-way houses in many Nigerian communities is what?

options.A: Deep-seated stigma and fear surrounding mental illness
options.B: An overabundance of available psychiatric rehabilitation beds
options.C: Complete public acceptance of medical disease models
options.D: Excessive funding from international health organizations

explanation: Stigma and misconceptions often cause communities to reject the placement of mental health facilities in their neighborhoods. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is an effective nursing intervention to counter community resistance against residential mental health homes?

options.A: Hiding the true purpose of the house from local leaders
options.B: Suing community members who voice complaints about the home
options.C: Isolating the facility behind high barbed-wire fences
options.D: Conducting community education and sensitization programs

explanation: Open education helps dispel myths, reduce fear, and promote community integration for recovering individuals. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h7)

question: What is a key component of a discharge plan for a half-way house resident?

options.A: A personalized relapse prevention strategy and trigger identification
options.B: Mandatory lifetime monitoring by armed security personnel
options.C: Immediate discontinuation of all outpatient support services
options.D: A legal contract promising never to visit a hospital again

explanation: Relapse prevention plans help clients recognize early warning signs and know who to contact during difficult moments. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h8)

question: How do healthcare teams determine if a resident is ready to leave the half-way house?

options.A: By waiting for a predetermined calendar year to expire automatically
options.B: By asking the local community to vote on the resident's departure
options.C: By checking if the resident has saved enough personal wealth
options.D: By evaluating their mastery of daily living skills and stability

explanation: Readiness for independent living is based on demonstrated functional competence, medication compliance, and emotional stability. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T4#GNS314_U5_T4_h8)
